questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the claim state that at least one rent payment has already been paid into deposit with the office designated by the canton?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the tenant claim compensation from the landlord for damage the defect caused to the tenant (for example damaged furniture or clothing, or extra costs)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord learned of the defect only orally, so that no written notice, written acknowledgement or inspection record of it exists?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim state that the tenant intends to pay the rent on deposit with the office designated by the canton instead of to the landlord, or has begun to do so?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that the rented dwelling has a defect (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails) or that the tenant is disturbed in using the dwelling as agreed, without the claim itself saying that the tenant alone caused the defect or must remedy it at his own expense?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord does not yet know of the defect (the tenant has not reported it and the landlord has not learned of it in another way)?

text:
Hi,

Since 13 April 2026 water has been coming in through the big living-room window of my flat at Brunnenrain 49 in Aarau every time it rains. It runs down the inside of the frame, collects on the sill and drips onto the parquet. After the heavy rain last week there was a puddle half a metre wide, and the wall under the window is now dark and soft to the touch. I've had to roll up the rug, move the sofa to the other side of the room and put towels down every evening when rain is forecast. The room smells musty and I don't like my daughter playing in there any more. My neighbour Nina Bucher says her window on the floor above looks fine, so it seems to be something about mine in particular, maybe the seal or the frame itself.

The rent for this flat is CHF 1900 a month, and I don't think it's right that Birkenrain Trading Ltd should get it while I live with buckets and towels. I intend to pay my rent into the official deposit account instead of to Birkenrain until the window has been properly repaired. A friend told me this is possible, but I've never done anything like it and want to be sure I get it right, so that it can't be used against me later.

Could you explain the steps I need to follow, and whether there's anything I must do before the next rent is due?

Many thanks,
Owen Shaw
